newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Cape branch of S.African ANC has 0.5 mln rand debt.
newsitem.headline: Cape branch of S.African ANC has 0.5 mln rand debt.

text.p: Telephones at the Western Cape branch of South Africa's ruling African National Congress were cut off for two weeks because of debts to various companies totalling about 500,000 rand ($180,000), a party spokesman said on Thursday.
"The debts were incurred during the 1994 general elections and some during last year's local government elections," ANC Western Cape spokesman Brent Simons said.
"We had to go without phones for two weeks, however we have negotiated with Telkom and the service was re-installed on Wednesday," he added.
Simons said the debts were for printing costs, vehicle rental, cellular phones and other expenses. The ANC intended to pay off the debts and had formed a fundraising committee.
In 1995 the Western Cape branch auctioned personal items of President Nelson Mandela, including the shoes he wore on the day of his release from jail, to raise funds to pay debts.
